ground_truth.unit: points on the 1-4 Only Means scale per point of Mate Competition (1-4)
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Mate Competition Predicts Support for Hate Crime"), column (1).  OLS of support for hate crime, the Only Means item ("When it comes to the refugee problem, violence is sometimes the only means that citizens have to get the attention of German politicians"; 1 = disagree strongly to 4 = agree strongly), on Mate Competition ("The inflow of refugees makes it more difficult for native men to find female partners"; same 1-4 scale), with no other regressors. Respondents of Wave 4 (December 2017) of the authors' online panel survey of German residents fielded by Respondi.  Conventional OLS standard errors in parentheses.

i4r.notes: Blanket I4R verdict (team 34, code reproduces the paper); no per-row entry for column 1.

ground_truth.unit: log-odds per unit of the male-to-female ratio
ground_truth.location: SI Table C1, column (5) Sum, Excess Males (Age 15 - 44)
ground_truth.context: SI Appendix C.1, Table C1 ("The Effect of Excess Males on the Probability of Observing at least One Hate Crime"), column (5), the Sum model plotted in main-text Figure 1.  Logistic regression across German municipalities of an indicator equal to one if the municipality saw at least one anti-refugee hate crime (arson or other attacks on refugee housing, or physical attacks on refugees, from the "Mut gegen rechte Gewalt" chronicle of the Amadeu Antonio Foundation and PRO ASYL) over 2015-2017, on Excess Males (the number of men divided by the number of women aged 15-44 in the municipality, 2015), controlling for log population, log population density, log unemployment rate, population change 2011-2015, AfD vote share 2013, and the county-level log refugee inflow (2014-2015), log refugee stock (2014), log general violence per capita, share highly educated, change in manufacturing share (2011-2015) and manufacturing share, plus Male Disadvantage (male over female unemployment rate), with state fixed effects. Municipalities in the top and bottom 2.5 percentiles of Excess Males are excluded.  Standard errors clustered by county.

i4r.notes: Blanket I4R verdict; no per-row entry for Table C1 column 5.

Same exclusion of extreme Excess Males values; standard errors clustered by county.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Table 1 'employment status' has no separate variable in survey.dta; the occupation factor (which mixes main activity and employment status, e.g. unemployed, retired, employee) is used for both.

Table 1 ordinal controls: income, occupation, religion, state, gender entered as factors (income keeps its 'No answer' category); self-assessed status (self_econ, code 11 recoded to 0) and household size (code minus 1) entered linearly; education = eduyrs (years), whose 11 missing Wave 4 values set N for cols 3-6.

Table 1 national/local batteries: the 8 ref_* and 8 ref_loc_* items entered linearly. Additional controls: contact_ind, distance_ref (factor incl. don't know), settle_ref (factor), afd, afd_ind, lrscale, muslim_ind.

Table C1: controls use the log versions provided in context.dta for population, density, refugee stock and violent crime (log_unemp_all_muni_2015 for unemployment); state fixed effects (per task description; the main text mentions county FE), plus year FE in the annual model; SEs clustered by ags_county; trimming at the 2.5/97.5 percentiles of Excess Males (15-44) computed across all municipalities with non-missing values before listwise deletion. Sum outcome = any Hate_all_muni over 2015-2017.
cell.notes: One exploratory run (attempt-1: variable inventory, no RESULT lines), then one scored run. Table 1: OLS of hate_violence_means on MateComp.cont etc. on Wave 4 respondents (lm, conventional SEs). Table C1 cols 5/6: fixest::feglm logit with state (and year) FE, clustered by county; glm with state dummies gives identical col 5 coefficient. Only 11 states remain in the context models after complete cases. No specification was tuned toward paper values.
